provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Native rule: crop the motif S (H rows x W cols; the generator makes it top-bottom symmetric with the 'pointer' axis horizontal). Build a (2W+H) square output. Put S unchanged in the left arm, rot-cw(S) in the top arm, the left-right mirror in the right arm and rot-ccw(S) in the bottom arm. Because S is top-bottom symmetric, the mirror equals rot180(S). So the native output is the union of the four 90-degree rotations about the centre of a canvas that holds S only in its left arm. Conjugating by any D4 element maps the rotation group to itself. In visible coordinates the rule therefore becomes: crop the motif S' and place it unchanged in arm T(left). Then overlay the 0/90/180/270 rotations of that canvas about its centre. Side bookkeeping: reversing rows sends left to right, and each clockwise turn advances left->top->right->bottom. So side = [left, top, right, bottom][(2*(d4>=4) + d4%4) % 4]. The arm length a is the motif extent along the arm direction. It is the cropped width for left/right and the cropped height for top/bottom. b is the other extent, and the output side is 2a+b. This also correctly handles square motifs (W==H). Background is the constant palette[0]. Interior background cells of the motif are copied as background, matching the generator.
draft_notes.limitations: Relies on the generator's guarantee that the motif is symmetric across its pointer axis, so the mirror copy equals the 180-degree rotation; the fixtures are consistent with this and no contradiction was found. The background is assumed to be palette[0], as in every generated scene. An input with no foreground pixels returns the input unchanged, which is outside the generator's domain. Not executed or tested by me.
